business.title: Cadonilimab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract malignancies: the phase II bicureX clinical trial
business.desc: Immune checkpoint inhibitors plus gemcitabine and cisplatin (GC) are standard first-line treatment for advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC). Here we report BicureX (ChiCTR2300073023), a single-centre, open-label, single-arm phase II trial of cadonilimab, an anti-PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific antibody, plus GC for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic BTC. Patients received up to eight combination cycles followed by cadonilimab maintenance. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumours version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1); secondary endpoints included disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DoR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and safety. Sixty-one patients were enrolled. At a median follow-up of 23.5 months, ORR was 55.7% (34/61; 95% confidence interval, 42.4–68.5%), meeting the prespecified Simon two-stage efficacy criterion. DCR was 85.2%, median DoR 6.1 months, PFS 8.0 months, and OS 15.6 months. Grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs) occurred in 68.9% and grade ≥3 immune-related adverse events (irAEs) in 18.0%; no death was adjudicated as treatment-related. Proteomics identified a post-hoc exploratory three-protein response-associated signal without significance after false discovery rate correction. These findings support further randomized evaluation. Response rates with approved chemoimmunotherapy regimens remain modest in patients with biliary tract cancer (BTC). Here the authors report the results of a phase II study testing the anti-PD1/CTLA4 bispecific antibody cadonilimab in combination with gemcitabine and cisplatin as first-line treatment for unresectable locally advanced or metastatic BTCs.

business.title: Microcapillary-assisted acoustoelectric platform for selective single-cell isolation and in situ transfection
business.desc: Single-cell transfection technologies hold tremendous promise for precision cell and immunotherapies. However, monolithic integration of cell isolation with targeted intracellular delivery remains technically challenging, especially within complex biological matrices. Herein, we present a microcapillary-assisted acoustoelectric single-cell selective isolation and sonoporative transfection platform (μC-ASSIST), which seamlessly sequences microcapillary-assisted dielectrophoresis (μC-DEP) for deterministic single-cell trapping with high-frequency surface acoustic waves (SAWs) for transient membrane poration within a unified workflow. We demonstrate the label-free, high-efficiency extraction of human non-small cell lung cancer (A549) cells from a complex white blood cell (WBC) background with a capture efficiency of 95%. Furthermore, we validate the highly efficient, contact-free intracellular delivery of diverse cargoes ranging from small dyes (PI) to functional small interfering RNA (siRNA) and large plasmid DNA (mRFP-C3), maintaining a high cell viability of 83.7% alongside a 78.1% transfection efficiency. Crucially, the targeted delivery of siBcl-xL significantly suppressed target mRNA expression and profoundly inhibited tumor cell motility. By circumventing off-target effects and cumbersome manual handling, the μC-ASSIST platform establishes a highly versatile, streamlined paradigm for precision single-cell engineering, holding immense potential for advancing functional genomics and next-generation gene therapies.

business.title: Focusing and weighing microanalytes in liquid enabled by higher-order piezoelectric resonant membranes
business.desc: Micro-electromechanical-system (MEMS) resonators have been recognized as powerful tools for precision mass detection. However, achieving both flexible on-chip capture of microanalytes and high-sensitivity liquid-phase sensing remains a technical challenge. We present a fully anchored multi-modal piezoelectric resonant membrane (PRM) that utilizes self-excited bulk acoustic waves to rapidly enrich sparsely dispersed microparticles within milliliter droplets and precisely locate them at the region of highest vibrational amplitude — the most sensitive area for resonance detection. The design of higher-order resonance modes preserves acoustofluidic enrichment performance while enabling reconfigurable particle distribution patterns through modulation of the acoustic field distribution. Experimental results demonstrate that the resonant frequency shift induced by the same mass load increases with the mode order, indicating that the sensing sensitivity is proportional to the resonance order. We systematically characterized the acoustofluidic parameters and electrical measurement performance of transverse modes from (0, 0) to (4, 0). This work shows that extending the integrated actuation-and-sense approach to consider multiple modes of resonances presents a toolbox for designing such miniaturized platforms to address nanogram-level mass analysis in liquid phase.

business.title: Towards advanced motion control systems for micro-scale magnetic drillers inside viscoelastic media
business.desc: Microrobotic systems have the potential to reach regions of the body with significantly less invasiveness than conventional surgical tools. However, control over clinically relevant workspaces remains challenging due to limitations in magnetic field and robotic trajectory control. Here, we present a planar eight-solenoid magnetic field generator (MFG) that enables programmable velocity and heading of a 250 × 250 × 1250 µm3 microscale driller through continuous field reorientation within a workspace of 20 × 20 × 20 cm3. The microscale driller achieved velocities up to 155 µm/s in 0.6 weight percent agarose gel, which mimics the mechanical properties of brain tissue, and executed turns beyond 90° with angular errors below 3°. These results demonstrate a scalable platform for precise and remote control of magnetically embedded microdevices, and support future development of minimally invasive systems for applications such as targeted therapeutic delivery and microsurgery.

business.title: An Accurate Land Cover Classification Map in China Integrating High-resolution Satellite Imagery and Planning Data with Deep Learning
business.desc: This study presents a planning-oriented high-resolution land cover dataset for China, developed to address the limitations of existing products in territorial spatial planning and regional land analysis. The dataset integrates 2-m optical satellite imagery with official planning maps using a deep learning semantic segmentation framework based on ConvNeXt. It includes six land cover classes—built-up areas, cropland, roads, green spaces, water bodies, and others—and is designed to better align remote-sensing outputs with planning-relevant land categories. We conducted a comprehensive validation using pixel-level test-set evaluation, point-based assessment with an open-access validation dataset, and nationwide areal consistency analysis against aggregated results from China’s Third National Land Survey. The product achieved competitive classification performance and showed the strongest agreement with official area statistics among the compared datasets, particularly for built-up areas, cropland, and roads. Visual comparisons further demonstrate clearer boundary delineation and more realistic spatial patterns in both urban and rural settings. As a planning-oriented baseline dataset, this product is particularly useful for built-up land accounting, cropland protection assessment, urban–rural spatial analysis, road-network extraction, and regional policy evaluation in situations where up-to-date survey data are unavailable. Its combination of high spatial resolution, strong semantic consistency, and nationwide coverage makes it valuable for both research and practical decision-making in China’s territorial spatial planning.

business.title: A transformer-enhanced U-Net with FiLM-driven clinical conditioning for multi-task breast ultrasound lesion analysis
business.desc: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide. Early and accurate detection of breast lesions using non-invasive imaging techniques is crucial for improving timely diagnosis, treatment outcomes, and patient prognosis. This study aims to develop and evaluate hybrid deep learning models for breast-lesion segmentation and classification in ultrasound images using patient-level cross-validation. Challenges such as low contrast, imaging artifacts, and irregular lesion morphology can limit accurate diagnosis, highlighting the need for advanced deep learning approaches for reliable breast-lesion analysis. Recent developments in deep learning, particularly hybrid architectures that combine convolutional and transformer representations, have shown promise in addressing these constraints. We present three Hybrid Deep Learning (HDL) models. Three complementary deep learning models were evaluated for breast lesion classification and segmentation using the Breast-Lesions-USG dataset. Model 1 employed DoubleHeadUNet with a ResNet-34 backbone, Model 2 combined a Swin V2 Transformer with a U-Net decoder, and Model 3 integrated a Hybrid Transformer-FiLM U-Net to incorporate clinical metadata. Patient-level five-fold cross-validation with strict patient separation and nested hyperparameter selection was employed. Model 1 achieved the highest accuracy (82.94%) and AUC (87.70%), while Model 3 demonstrated the highest malignant recall (81.63%) and strongest segmentation performance (Dice: 0.901; IoU: 0.825). Model 2 achieved an accuracy of 79.76% and an AUC of 87.54%. Statistical analysis indicated that most accuracy differences were not significant, supporting the complementary strengths of the three models rather than identifying a universally superior approach. Comparisons with previous studies were considered indicative due to differences in datasets and evaluation protocols.
